procedure.title: Fixing `never` Types
procedure.step: Search the codebase for variables or expressions inferred as never. Look for "// ! NEVER" flags.
Identify the cause: — Exhaustive switch without a matching case. — Unreachable code after a type guard. — Incorrect union narrowing that eliminates all types.
Remove the "// ! NEVER" flag once resolved.

procedure.title: Fixing `unknown` Types
procedure.step: Search for "// ! UNKNOWN" flags or unknown typed variables.
Determine the actual runtime type (via API docs, console.log, etc.).

Alternatively, if the type is known with certainty, use a type assertion:
const data = response.data as TaskResponse;
Remove the "// ! UNKNOWN" flag once resolved.

procedure.title: Declaring Nested Iterable Types
procedure.step: Count the nesting depth of the array.

For depth ≥3, use alternating generic syntax:
const cube: Array<Array<string[]>[]> = [];
Ensure each element type is explicitly declared — no implicit any[].

procedure.title: Separating Type Declarations
procedure.step: Identify all inline interface / type declarations in implementation files.
Create a types module (e.g., types/task.ts) in the same feature folder.

Update the implementation file to import:
import type { Task } from "./types/task";
Use import type for type-only imports to enable tree-shaking.

procedure.title: Handling Async Return Types
procedure.step:
For async functions, annotate with Promise<void>:
async function loadData(): Promise<void> { /* … */ }

For non-async functions, annotate with : void:
function handleClick(): void { /* … */ }
Prefer manual annotation over suppression — only suppress as a last resort.
